Then into the people Harry seduces: a repressed moneyman, his trustafarian singer sister, their huge-haired Jewish mum. The characterisations are broad and the larky tone is set by the opening line: “I could always do an immaculate English accent.
All in all, it feels hard to justify a top ticket price of £195 for this minimally staged, 80-minute one-man Broadway import.
Not since Dick van Dyke in Mary Poppins have we had to endure such excruciating dissonance.

Billy Crudup is a sensation, successfully playing all of the characters and managing to give each one a distinct personality, along with fascinating physical attributes.

cn.t: Crudup delivers a virtuoso performance in this identity-deception tale, but critics split on the meandering script. Some praise the witty, darkly entertaining monologue, while others find it thin and question the protagonist's dubious English accent.
